user.title: Set up MQTT
user.description: HomeKey Household uses the official Home Assistant MQTT integration as its transport. MQTT is not configured yet — choose how you want to continue.

mqtt_guide.title: Configure MQTT
mqtt_guide.description:
Install and configure the official MQTT integration, then come back and press Submit.

1. Go to [Settings → Devices & Services](/config/integrations).
2. Click **Add Integration** and choose **MQTT**.
3. Enter your broker host/port (and credentials if required) and finish the wizard.
4. Press **Submit** below to re-check the connection.

The integration is a pure consumer of the firmware MQTT topics; the broker can be Mosquitto or any MQTT broker.

Documentation: {docs}

mqtt_express.title: Configure MQTT automatically
mqtt_express.description:
Enter your broker details. HomeKey Household will create the official MQTT integration entry for you.

Use the MQTT protocol version 5 (the default; the firmware is also compatible with 3.1.1). Host 127.0.0.1 is only correct if the broker runs on the same host as Home Assistant.

mqtt_addon.title: Use the MQTT add-on
mqtt_addon.description:
Install and start the official Mosquitto broker add-on via Supervisor, then wire up the MQTT integration automatically.

This needs no broker details. It is available only on Home Assistant OS or a Supervised installation, because only there can Supervisor install the add-on. Press **Submit** to continue.

household.title: HomeKey Household
household.description:
Configure a HomeKey household. MQTT is reused from the Home Assistant MQTT integration.

All fields below are editable — the values are prefilled from the device/MQTT discovery where possible, but you can change any of them before submitting.

data_description.household_id: Matches the household_id published on the household MQTT topics, e.g. HOME-001.
data_description.recovery_secret: Used only to derive the HMAC command key. Never sent over MQTT and never stored by Home Assistant. Example format: 24359u234fhurbgerbvuiebvubervbvun. Keep a copy in a safe place (e.g. your password manager) — Home Assistant does not keep it, so if you lose it you cannot re-derive the command key.
data_description.salt: The salt the firmware uses when deriving the command key, if one is configured. Leave empty if the firmware uses no salt.
data_description.command_control: When disabled the lock entity is read-only. Commands fail closed without a credential.

error.invalid_household_id: Household ID must be 1-64 characters of [A-Za-z0-9_-].
error.invalid_recovery_secret: The recovery secret must not be empty.
error.mqtt_not_configured: MQTT is still not configured or not connected. Finish the MQTT setup, then try again.
error.mqtt_setup_failed: Could not create the MQTT integration automatically. Please add the MQTT integration manually from Settings → Devices & Services, then try again.
error.cannot_connect: Home Assistant could not reach the MQTT broker at that address. Check the host and port, and make sure the broker is running and reachable from this machine. Note: 127.0.0.1 only works if the broker runs on the same host as Home Assistant.
error.mqtt_addon_failed: Could not install or start the Mosquitto broker add-on. Check Supervisor, then try again or use the express setup instead.
error.mqtt_addon_unavailable: Supervisor did not offer the Mosquitto broker add-on for installation. Install the 'Mosquitto broker' add-on from Settings → Add-ons, start it, then choose this option again — or use the express setup instead.
error.addon_info_failed: Supervisor could not read the Mosquitto broker add-on's information. Open Settings → Add-ons → Mosquitto broker and check that it is installed correctly, then try again.
error.addon_connection_failed: The Mosquitto broker add-on did not come up in time. Open Settings → Add-ons → Mosquitto broker, confirm it is running, then try again. If it keeps failing, check the add-on's own log for errors.
error.addon_start_failed: The Mosquitto broker add-on started, but Home Assistant could not connect to it. Open the add-on's Log tab and fix any startup errors (for example, a port conflict or a broken configuration), then try again. Using the express setup with your own broker credentials also works.

abort.not_hassio: The MQTT add-on option is only available on Home Assistant OS or a Supervised installation.
